text: 'Tis acting for one's particular reputation and profit, not for the public good, to refer that to be done in the public squares which one may do in the council chamber; and to noon day what might have been done the night before; and to be jealous to do that himself which his colleague can do as well as he.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book III, Chapter X, Of Managing the Will
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
